planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in deep, fertile, constantly moist soil in partial shade, sheltered from cold drying winds; 'Maurice Mason' is prized for wrinkled, glossy leaves that emerge a rich chocolate-bronze before settling to mid-green.

directions: Plant divisions in deep, humus-rich, reliably moist soil in partial shade, ideally at a pond edge or streamside where roots never dry out. 'Maurice Mason' produces wrinkled, glossy, mid-green leaves strongly flushed chocolate-bronze as they emerge in spring, held on an upright, clump-forming crown. Dark red flowering stems carry dense, plume-like panicles of small, star-shaped, rose-pink flowers in early to midsummer, followed by attractive red seed heads that extend interest into fall. Mulch well and shield from wind to prevent the bold foliage from scorching, and divide congested clumps in early spring every three to four years to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in fertile, constantly moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; 'Alba' is the white-flowered form of featherleaf rodgersia, its pure white plumes a striking contrast against the bronze-tinted young foliage.

directions: Plant divisions in deep, fertile, humus-rich soil that stays consistently moist, in partial shade or full sun where soil moisture is assured. 'Alba' forms a bold clump of palmate leaves divided into jaggedly toothed leaflets that open bronze in spring and mature to a deep, dark green. Tall, upright flower spikes carry dense panicles of small, star-shaped, linen-white flowers in midsummer, giving a cooler, brighter accent than the pink- and red-flowered rodgersia cultivars. Keep soil from drying out to prevent leaf scorch, mulch generously, and divide crowded clumps in early spring every few years to refresh vigor and flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade, or full sun at a waterside site; 'Fireworks' bears especially large, glowing deep-pink flower plumes over a big mound of green leaves edged in bronze.

directions: Plant divisions in deep, fertile, reliably moist to boggy soil in partial shade, or in full sun only where the roots stay constantly wet. 'Fireworks' is a large, imposing selection with broad mounds of green foliage edged in bronze, sending up tall, sturdy stems topped with big, glowing deep-pink plumes in early summer that read from a distance. It is one of the showiest-flowering rodgersia cultivars available and pairs well with bold hostas and ligularias at a pond or stream margin. Mulch to conserve moisture, avoid letting the soil dry out even briefly, and divide overgrown clumps in early spring to maintain a tidy, floriferous crown.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in deep, constantly moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; 'Kupfermond' was a top performer in the Chicago Botanic Garden's decade-long rodgersia trial, noted for its reliably bushy habit and chameleon-like foliage color.

directions: Plant divisions in deep, fertile, consistently moist to wet soil in partial shade, along a pond edge or stream bank where the large rhizomes have room to spread. 'Kupfermond' ('copper moon') is a robust hybrid selection whose deeply furrowed leaves emerge a rich red-bronze in spring, fade toward green tinged with bronze by midspring, pick up bronzy margins in summer, and turn red again in fall. In late spring, clusters of pale pink flowers with creamy-white stamens are carried on flowering spikes well above the foliage, on plants that mature into an exceptionally full, wide-spreading clump. Give it ample space and steady moisture, since it is one of the largest and bushiest rodgersia selections in cultivation, and mulch well to prevent the bold leaves from scorching in drier spells.
